name: control-panel-runtime-foundation
executionConcern: Control Panel root bootstrap, providers, global styles, shell/navigation, BFF/service proxy and server/session composition
objective: Establish one fail-closed Control Panel runtime foundation before any section-specific repair, with no local domain truth and no client-selected trusted context.
truthOwner: Control Panel owns composition/transport only; Identity owns session identity and each sovereign service owns its domain state.

tasks.objective: Close root bootstrap, shell and navigation composition
tasks.currentProblem: The prior package did not explicitly cover app root providers/styles and treated navigation as the main section inventory, allowing cross-cutting defects to survive section repairs.
tasks.requiredChange: Trace root layout/page/providers, shell layout, navigation/top bar and global styles; remove duplicate or fallback truth; ensure every route enters the same authenticated shell and renders explicit loading/forbidden/error states.
tasks.targetState: All Control Panel routes share one deterministic bootstrap, shell and RTL/accessibility foundation with no hidden alternate truth path.
tasks.action: Repair the earliest composition defect, migrate callers to one source, remove obsolete duplicate paths and verify route inventory against current BB.
mustNotChange: Do not add local mock/fallback business truth.
Do not authorize a route solely because it is visible in navigation.
Do not broaden into unrelated surfaces.
acceptanceCriteria: Root and shell composition is single-source and deterministic.
Every current section and hidden route remains reachable only through intended routing/access behavior.
RTL, focus, loading, forbidden and error states remain explicit.
tasks.rollback: Revert the focused foundation commit or roll forward to the last known single composition path; never restore duplicate truth.
tasks.commitBoundary: One focused runtime-foundation commit after obsolete composition paths are removed and foundation checks pass.

tasks.objective: Close BFF proxy, server session and upstream routing boundary
tasks.currentProblem: Auth/service proxies and server adapters are shared by multiple sovereign owners; permissive routing or forwarded client context would undermine every section.
tasks.requiredChange: Prove explicit service routing, cookie/session handling, authorization-header behavior, error propagation, timeout/unavailable classification and stripping/derivation of trusted context at the server boundary.
tasks.targetState: The BFF transports authenticated intent to approved owners, rejects unsupported services and never converts client-controlled identity/scope input into trust.
tasks.action: Trace api routes through server adapters to upstream configuration, correct the root boundary, add focused negative tests and remove bypass adapters.
mustNotChange: Do not expose raw tokens or credentials to browser logs/errors.
Do not create a generic open proxy.
Do not hide upstream errors with synthetic success.
acceptanceCriteria: Trusted identity/scope comes from server-authoritative session/service context.
Dependency failure and response status are preserved for section recovery logic.
tasks.rollback: Restore the prior secure proxy boundary only if it remains fail-closed; otherwise roll forward at the same boundary.
tasks.commitBoundary: One focused BFF/server commit with targeted tests and no unrelated domain changes.
